subject: showering in space
title: What If You Took a Shower in Space?

scenes.text: What if you took a shower in space? The water would never reach the floor.
In orbit, water doesn't flow down a drain. It floats in blobs, clings to skin, and can drift into electronics.
NASA tried anyway. In 1973, Skylab got a shower: a fold-up cylinder, foot restraints, and about six pints of water.
Every drop had to be vacuumed back up. A full shower took more than two hours from start to finish.
So today's space station has no shower at all. Astronauts use wet cloths, no-rinse shampoo and towels.
And none of it is wasted: the station recycles over ninety percent of its wastewater. Yesterday's wash becomes tomorrow's drinking water.
